lines: Four channel stereo mixer with pan, mute, solo, two stereo aux buses and CV over level, pan and mute, expandable with ExFor and ExTwo modules placed to its left
Sets the level of the main stereo output, with an audio taper and up to 6dB of gain fully clockwise
Silences the main stereo output, with a smoothing filter that stops the cut from clicking
Sets that channel's level on an audio taper: logarithmic over the top three quarters, -18dB at a quarter turn, and straight down to silence below that
Pans that channel between the left and right main outputs on an equal-power law
Silences that channel, with a smoothing filter that stops the cut from clicking; a solo on any channel overrides it
Plays that channel alone and clears the solo on the others; control-click, or command-click on a Mac, adds the channel to the solo instead of replacing it
Sets how much of that channel is mixed into aux bus 1, taken after the level, pan and mute controls unless the menu switches send 1 to pre-fader
Sets how much of that channel is mixed into aux bus 2, taken after the level, pan and mute controls unless the menu switches send 2 to pre-fader
Sets the level of the aux bus 1 return as it is mixed into the main output, with an audio taper and up to 6dB of gain fully clockwise
Sets the level of the aux bus 2 return as it is mixed into the main output, with an audio taper and up to 6dB of gain fully clockwise
The channel's audio input; a polyphonic cable is mixed down to mono and the level normalised
Scales that channel's level, 0V silencing it and 10V leaving the level knob alone, smoothed so that fast changes do not click
Shifts that channel's pan, 5V moving it fully right and -5V fully left, added to the pan knob and smoothed so that fast changes do not click
Mutes that channel while the voltage is above 1.6V and un-mutes it below 0.8V, or toggles the mute on each rising edge when the menu is set that way
Returns aux bus 1 from whatever the send feeds, scaled by the R1 knob and mixed into the main output
Returns aux bus 2 from whatever the send feeds, scaled by the R2 knob and mixed into the main output
The main stereo mix, after the master level knob and master mute
That channel's own signal after its level knob and mute, carrying no pan and none of the other channels
The sum of every channel's aux 1 send, for patching to an effect whose output comes back at the R1 jacks
The sum of every channel's aux 2 send, for patching to an effect whose output comes back at the R2 jacks
Menu — Send 1 Pre Fader and Send 2 Pre Fader take that bus's sends from before the level and pan controls, so mute and solo apply but the fader does not
Menu — Mute CV toggles on/off makes each rising edge at a mute CV jack flip the mute, in place of muting while the gate is high
Note — the settings on the context menu apply only to the four channels of the module you right-clicked; each expander keeps its own
squinkylabs-mixm.notes: Params 27, 28, 31-36 are hidden state carrying the menu settings and the mute and solo states, and have no control on the panel.

lines: Expander adding four mono channels to the Form mixer, placed anywhere to the left of it, carrying the main stereo bus, both aux buses and the solo bus without patch cables
Sets that channel's level on an audio taper: logarithmic over the top three quarters, -18dB at a quarter turn, and straight down to silence below that
Pans that channel between the left and right main outputs on an equal-power law
Silences that channel, with a smoothing filter that stops the cut from clicking; a solo on any channel of the chain overrides it
Plays that channel alone and clears the solo on every other channel of the chain; control-click, or command-click on a Mac, adds the channel to the solo instead of replacing it
Sets how much of that channel is mixed into aux bus 1, taken after the level, pan and mute controls unless the menu switches send 1 to pre-fader
Sets how much of that channel is mixed into aux bus 2, taken after the level, pan and mute controls unless the menu switches send 2 to pre-fader
The channel's audio input; a polyphonic cable is mixed down to mono and the level normalised
Scales that channel's level, 0V silencing it and 10V leaving the level knob alone, smoothed so that fast changes do not click
Shifts that channel's pan, 5V moving it fully right and -5V fully left, added to the pan knob and smoothed so that fast changes do not click
Mutes that channel while the voltage is above 1.6V and un-mutes it below 0.8V, or toggles the mute on each rising edge when the menu is set that way
That channel's own signal after its level knob and mute, carrying no pan and none of the other channels
Menu — Send 1 Pre Fader and Send 2 Pre Fader take that bus's sends from before the level and pan controls, so mute and solo apply but the fader does not
Menu — Mute CV toggles on/off makes each rising edge at a mute CV jack flip the mute, in place of muting while the gate is high
Note — with no Form mixer in the chain the four channels work on their own, each mixing a polyphonic input to mono and acting as a VCA with mute and solo
squinkylabs-mix4.notes: Params 16, 25-31 are hidden state carrying the menu settings and the mute and solo states. The panel prints no row labels of its own; the rows line up with the labels on the Form mixer.

lines: Expander adding two stereo channels to the Form mixer, placed anywhere to the left of it, carrying the main stereo bus, both aux buses and the solo bus without patch cables
Sets that channel's level on an audio taper: logarithmic over the top three quarters, -18dB at a quarter turn, and straight down to silence below that
Sets the balance of that stereo channel, full left giving the left side full gain and silencing the right, and centre attenuating both by 6dB
Silences that channel, with a smoothing filter that stops the cut from clicking; a solo on any channel of the chain overrides it
Plays that channel alone and clears the solo on every other channel of the chain; control-click, or command-click on a Mac, adds the channel to the solo instead of replacing it
Sets how much of that channel is mixed into aux bus 1, taken after the level, balance and mute controls unless the menu switches send 1 to pre-fader
Sets how much of that channel is mixed into aux bus 2, taken after the level, balance and mute controls unless the menu switches send 2 to pre-fader
The left input of that stereo channel; patched on its own it feeds both sides, and the balance control then pans it between the two direct outputs
The right input of that stereo channel; left unpatched, the left input feeds both sides
Scales that channel's level, 0V silencing it and 10V leaving the level knob alone, smoothed so that fast changes do not click
Shifts that channel's balance, 5V moving it fully right and -5V fully left, added to the balance knob and smoothed so that fast changes do not click
Mutes that channel while the voltage is above 1.6V and un-mutes it below 0.8V, or toggles the mute on each rising edge when the menu is set that way
The left side of that channel after its level knob and mute, carrying none of the other channels
The right side of that channel after its level knob and mute, carrying none of the other channels
Menu — Send 1 Pre Fader and Send 2 Pre Fader take that bus's sends from before the level and balance controls, so mute and solo apply but the fader does not
Menu — Mute CV toggles on/off makes each rising edge at a mute CV jack flip the mute, in place of muting while the gate is high
squinkylabs-mixStereo.notes: Params 8, 13-17 are hidden state carrying the menu settings and the mute and solo states. The panel prints no row labels of its own; the rows line up with the labels on the Form mixer.

lines: Eight channel stereo mixer with pan, mute, solo and an aux send on every channel, a stereo aux bus, and an expansion input for chaining a second mixer into the output
Sets the level of the main stereo output, straight gain from silence to unity
Silences the main stereo output, with a smoothing filter that stops the cut from clicking
Sets that channel's level, straight gain from silence to unity with no taper applied, despite the manual describing a tapered response
Pans that channel between the left and right main outputs on an equal-power law
Silences that channel, with a smoothing filter that stops the cut from clicking; a solo on any channel overrides it
Plays that channel alone and clears the solo on the others; control-click, or command-click on a Mac, adds the channel to the solo instead of replacing it
Sets how much of that channel is mixed into the stereo aux bus, taken after the level and pan controls
Sets the level of the aux return as it is mixed into the main output, straight gain from silence to unity
The channel's audio input
Scales that channel's level, 0V silencing it and 10V leaving the level knob alone, smoothed so that fast changes do not click
Shifts that channel's pan, 5V moving it fully right and -5V fully left, added to the pan knob and smoothed so that fast changes do not click
Mutes that channel while the voltage is above 2V, smoothed so that a sharp gate does not click
An expansion input, mixed straight into the main output with no level, pan or mute of its own, for taking the output of a second mixer
Returns the aux bus from whatever the send feeds, scaled by the R knob and mixed into the main output
The main stereo mix, after the master level knob and master mute
That channel's own signal after its level knob and mute, carrying no pan and none of the other channels
The sum of every channel's aux send, for patching to an effect whose output comes back at the R jacks
squinkylabs-mix8.notes: The manual says the channel volume uses the tapered response of the AS mixer, but the composite multiplies by the knob value directly, with no taper lookup, so the line follows the code. The mute CV here has a single 2V threshold with no hysteresis and no toggle mode, unlike the Form mixer. Panel labels are drawn at runtime and are not in the panel artwork; they were read from the widget source.

lines: Precision VCO in 3HP putting out one waveform at a time, with octave, semitone and fine pitch knobs, attenuverters on both modulation inputs, and polyphony taken from the v/oct input
Sets the base octave, 0 to 10, with 4 putting 0V at the v/oct input on C4 at 261.63Hz
Transposes the pitch by up to 11 semitones either way, despite the manual saying 12
Tunes the pitch a semitone up or down
Picks the waveform: sine, triangle, saw, square, even, pure sine or pure triangle, in that order; the tooltip names the one selected
Sets the pulse width, 0 to 100%, with an audible effect only on the square wave
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the fm input, on an audio taper that gives fine control of small amounts, and passes none of it at centre
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the pwm input before it is added to the pulse width knob
Sets the pitch, a volt per octave; the number of channels on this cable sets how many voices run, and one voice runs with nothing patched
Modulates the pulse width through the pwm attenuverter; a monophonic cable modulates every voice, a polyphonic one modulates a voice per channel
Bends the pitch exponentially through the fm attenuverter
The selected waveform, polyphonic with one channel per voice
squinkylabs-basic.notes: The manual says the semitone knob transposes by up to 12 semitones; the composite configures it as plus or minus 11, which the line follows.

lines: Three VCOs on one panel, each with its own pitch offsets, waveform and mixing level, with separate outputs and a mixed output, and hard sync from VCO 1 to either of the others
Sets the base octave for that VCO over a ten octave range, with the number shown above the knob
Transposes that VCO by up to 12 semitones either way, shown as a note name while its V/oct jack is patched and as the interval from the VCO it tracks while it is not
Tunes that VCO a semitone up or down
Attenuates the CV at the Fm jack for that VCO, which bends the pitch exponentially and suits vibrato rather than FM synthesis
Sets the pulse width for that VCO, with an audible effect only while its square wave is selected
Attenuates the CV at the Pwm jack for that VCO before it is added to the pulse width knob
Picks the waveform for that VCO: sine, triangle, saw, square, even, or off, which silences it without unpatching anything
Hard-syncs that VCO to VCO 1, restarting its cycle from the saw wave of VCO 1
Sets how much of that VCO goes into the mixed output, with no effect on that VCO's own output jack
Sets the pitch of that VCO, a volt per octave; left unpatched, the VCO takes its pitch from the nearest patched V/oct jack above it
Bends the pitch of that VCO through its Mod knob; left unpatched, it takes the signal from the nearest patched Fm jack above it
Modulates the pulse width of that VCO through its pwm knob; left unpatched, it takes the signal from the nearest patched Pwm jack above it
That VCO's waveform on its own, at full level, untouched by the mixing knobs
The three VCOs added together at the levels set by the mixing knobs, scaled back to a 10V peak when those levels total more than full scale; the plus signs turn green while that is happening
squinkylabs-ev3.notes: Param 7 is named unused in the composite and has no control on the panel.

lines: VCO with sine, triangle, saw and square outputs all available at once, forked from Fundamental VCO-1 to use a quarter of the CPU; the maker deprecated it once VCV rewrote the original
Switches between the digital waveforms and an analogue emulation that softens the sine and adds a little random detuning
Picks the oscillator sync a signal at the sync input triggers, hard or soft
Sets the pitch, plus or minus 54 semitones from C4
Tunes the pitch a semitone up or down
Attenuates the CV at the fm input, which bends the pitch exponentially
Sets the pulse width of the square output, with no effect on the other three waveforms
Attenuates the CV at the pwm input before it is added to the pulse width knob
Sets the pitch, a volt per octave
Bends the pitch through the fm cv knob
Restarts the oscillator's cycle, hard or soft according to the switch
Modulates the pulse width of the square output through the pwm cv knob
The sine wave
The triangle wave
The saw wave
The square wave, at the width set by the p width knob
Emulation of the Roland JP-8000 Super Saw: seven saw oscillators tracking one pitch, with control over how far they spread and how loud the detuned ones are, polyphonic and optionally stereo
Transposes the pitch in octaves, five down to four up, with the setting shown above the knob
Transposes the pitch by up to 11 semitones either way, with the note name shown above the knob
Tunes the pitch a semitone up or down
Attenuates the CV at the FM input, which bends the pitch
Spreads the pitch of the seven saws apart, the middle one staying on pitch while the other six move above and below it, following the response of the JP-8000
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Detune input before it is added to the Detune knob
Sets the level of the six detuned saws against the middle one, which is alone at the bottom of the knob's travel, following the response of the JP-8000
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Mix input before it is added to the Mix knob
Picks the alias reduction: Classic emulates the original, with a highpass filter tuned to the oscillator and no treatment of the highs; Clean 1 oversamples four times, Clean 2 sixteen
Sets the pitch, a volt per octave; the number of channels on this cable sets how many voices run
Randomises the phase of all seven saws on every rising edge, which stops repeated notes from sounding identical
Spreads the saws apart through the trim knob below the Detune control
Sets the level of the detuned saws through the trim knob below the Mix control
Bends the pitch through the FM knob
The left side of the stereo output; with the right output also patched the seven saws are panned across the stereo field, and with this jack alone all seven come out of it
The right side of the stereo output, carrying its share of the saws panned across the stereo field; patched on its own it carries the whole sound
Menu — Hard Pan sends six of the seven saws entirely to one side or the other in stereo, and does nothing when only one output is patched
Subharmonic VCO after the Moog Subharmonicon: two oscillators, each with two subharmonics at a whole-number division of its pitch, all six mixed to one output, with a quantizer on the pitch input
Sets the base octave for that oscillator and for the two subharmonics taken from it, 0 to 10
Transposes that oscillator and its subharmonics by up to 11 semitones either way
Tunes that oscillator and its subharmonics a semitone up or down
Picks the waveform for that side: Saw, Sq for a pulse at the width set by the PW knob, or Mix, which gives a pulse on the fundamental and a saw on the two subharmonics
Sets the level of that oscillator's fundamental in the mix, on an audio taper
Sets the level of that oscillator's first subharmonic in the mix, on an audio taper
Sets the level of that oscillator's second subharmonic in the mix, on an audio taper
Sets the pulse width for that side, 0 to 100%, and has an audible effect where the waveform is Sq or Mix
Divides that oscillator's frequency to make its first subharmonic, a whole number from 1 to 16, so 3 puts the subharmonic at a third of the fundamental frequency
Divides that oscillator's frequency to make its second subharmonic, a whole number from 1 to 16
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the pulse width jack below it before it is added to the PW knob
Picks the quantizer on the V/Oct input: Off, 12ET or 7ET for equal temperament, 12JI or 7JI for justly intoned scales; every scale is built on C, so another key needs the CV offset and tuning back
Sets the pitch of both oscillators and all four subharmonics, a volt per octave through the quantizer; the number of channels on this cable sets how many voices run
Shifts the divisor of that subharmonic, 10V moving it by the full 1 to 16 range, and the result is rounded to a whole number
Nothing in the module reads this control; the CV at that subharmonic's tune jack is scaled by its divisor knob instead
Modulates the pulse width on that side through the trim knob above it
Scales the level of that oscillator in the mix: 10V leaves the level knob alone and 0V silences it
The six oscillators mixed together
Menu — AGC works as a hard peak limiter on the mix, holding the level once several oscillators are turned up, and is worth leaving off while the mixing CV inputs are being modulated
squinkylabs-sub.notes: Params 8, 9, 10 and 11, the four trim knobs under the Div A and Div B controls, are left with no line: computeDivisorSub in composites/Sub.h is called with the divisor knob passed as both the knob and the trim, so these four params are never read and the subharmonic tune CV is scaled by the divisor knob instead. Param 27 is the AGC menu setting and has no control on the panel.

lines: Polyphonic sine VCO with through-zero linear FM, a wave shaper, an ADSR and a set of VCAs, able to fold or morph its wave and to be hard-synced
Sets the base pitch in octaves, 0 to 10
Multiplies the base pitch by a whole number, 1 to 16, which is how the carrier is set against the modulator in an FM patch, despite the manual giving only 1, 2 and 3
Tunes the pitch up or down by as much as an octave
Picks what the wave shaper does: sine leaves the sine wave alone, fold runs it through a wave folder, and T/S morphs between triangle and saw
Sets the output level, which is the FM depth when this output feeds the LFM input of another Kitchen Sink
Sets the depth of the through-zero linear FM, and scales the CV at the Depth jack and the ADSR where those are in play
Sets how much of the oscillator's own sine wave is fed back into its modulation input, which thickens the timbre without a second oscillator
Sets the wave shaping: how much folding in fold, and how far from triangle towards saw in T/S; the sine setting ignores it
Applies the internal ADSR to the output level, multiplying with the Level knob
Applies the internal ADSR to the linear FM depth, multiplying with the Depth knob
Applies the internal ADSR to the feedback amount, multiplying with the Fdbk knob
Applies the internal ADSR to the wave shape, multiplying with the Shape knob
Adds Moog-style snap to the internal ADSR: 0 for a plain envelope, 1 for a little snap, 2 for more, which gives the envelope something of an AHDSR shape without setting a hold time
Sets the attack time of the internal ADSR
Sets the decay time of the internal ADSR
Sets the sustain level of the internal ADSR
Sets the release time of the internal ADSR
Attenuates the CV at the FM jack, which bends the pitch exponentially and suits vibrato
Opens the internal ADSR while the gate is high, one channel per voice
Sets the pitch, a volt per octave; the number of channels on this cable sets how many voices run
Bends the pitch exponentially through the FM attenuverter above it
The modulator input for through-zero linear FM, its depth set by the Depth knob; with nothing patched here the only FM available is the feedback path
Restarts the oscillator's cycle on each cycle of the signal patched here, giving the classic sync sound, and works best with a signal lower in pitch than this oscillator
Scales the linear FM depth, multiplying with the Depth knob
Scales the feedback amount, multiplying with the Fdbk knob
Scales the wave shaping, multiplying with the Shape knob
The oscillator after the wave shaper and the output level, polyphonic with one channel per voice
Menu — Hookup Modulator appears when another Kitchen Sink is directly to the left, and patches that one up as the FM modulator for this one
Menu — Envelope "Snap" and Extra Envelope "Snap" set the same snap shaping as the Snap control on the panel
squinkylabs-wvco.notes: Param 18, the second snap setting, and param 19, a patch version number, have no control on the panel. The manual says the Ratio knob goes 1, 2, 3; the composite configures it 1 to 16.

lines: Waveshaper VCO: a sine oscillator with linear FM, driven through a folder and clipper into ten Chebyshev waveshapers, which gives a level control and a CV input for each of the first ten harmonics
Sets the base octave of the sine oscillator over a ten octave range, with the octave number shown above the knob
Transposes the sine oscillator by up to 11 semitones either way, with the note name shown above the knob
Tunes the sine oscillator a semitone up or down
Attenuates the CV at the Mod jack, which bends the pitch exponentially and gives inharmonic timbres at audio rates
Sets the depth of through-zero linear FM from the signal at the LFM jack, which keeps the harmonics in tune as the depth changes
Picks what the stage in front of the waveshapers does with a signal over one volt: Fold runs it through a wave folder, Clip hard-clips it
Drives the folder or clipper harder, and combines with the Gain CV and the EG input; the waveshapers give exact harmonics only at a gain of exactly 1, which the Preset button restores
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Gain jack before it is combined with the Gain knob
Sets the level of that waveshaper's harmonic in the output mix
Scales all the even harmonics together, leaving the fundamental alone, and passes the individual harmonic levels untouched when fully up
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Even jack before it is added to the Even knob
Scales all the odd harmonics together, leaving the fundamental alone, and passes the individual harmonic levels untouched when fully up
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Odd jack before it is added to the Odd knob
Rolls off the upper harmonics, 18dB per octave fully counter-clockwise and flat fully clockwise
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Slope jack before it is added to the Slope knob
Sets the rise time of the lag generators on all ten harmonic level CV inputs, which are exponential and share this setting
Sets the fall time of the lag generators on all ten harmonic level CV inputs, which are exponential and share this setting
Sets the pitch of the sine oscillator, a volt per octave
Bends the pitch exponentially through the Mod knob
The modulator input for through-zero linear FM, its depth set by the LFM knob
Sets the level of that harmonic through the lag generator set by the Rise and Fall knobs, multiplying with the knob beside it
Drives the gain of the stage feeding the waveshapers, through the trim knob below the Gain control; an envelope patched here shifts the timbre rather than the output level
Replaces the internal sine oscillator as the source fed to the folder, clipper and waveshapers; precise harmonic control needs the internal oscillator instead
Combines with the Gain knob to drive the folder or clipper, so a 0-10V envelope here sweeps the timbre from dull to bright
Scales all the even harmonics through the Even trim knob
Scales all the odd harmonics through the Odd trim knob
Rolls off the upper harmonics through the Slope trim knob
Lengthens the rise time of the lag generators on the harmonic level inputs, added to the Rise knob
Lengthens the fall time of the lag generators on the harmonic level inputs, added to the Fall knob
The ten waveshapers mixed together
Note — the Preset button steps between the fundamental alone, all ten harmonics up, and your own earlier setting, and always resets the gain to exactly 1, which is what precise harmonics need
Note — the clip lamp is green while there is signal and red while the folder or clipper is working
squinkylabs-CHB2.notes: Param 20 is named unused and input 17 has no position on the panel; neither is given a line. The Preset button is a widget rather than a parameter, so it has no tag of its own.

lines: Polyphonic organ voice after the Hammond tone-wheel organs: nine drawbars mixing fixed sine partials, percussion, key click and its own envelopes, so it needs no VCA or filter after it
Sets the level of the 16' sine, an octave below the fundamental, which sounds C3 when the fundamental is C4; a step of the drawbar is about 3dB
Sets the level of the 5 1/3' sine, a fifth above the fundamental, which sounds G4 when the fundamental is C4; a step of the drawbar is about 3dB
Sets the level of the 8' sine, the fundamental itself at C4; a step of the drawbar is about 3dB
Sets the level of the 4' sine, the second harmonic, which sounds C5 when the fundamental is C4; a step of the drawbar is about 3dB
Sets the level of the 2 2/3' sine, the third harmonic, which sounds G5 when the fundamental is C4; a step of the drawbar is about 3dB
Sets the level of the 2' sine, the fourth harmonic, which sounds C6 when the fundamental is C4; a step of the drawbar is about 3dB
Sets the level of the 1 3/5' sine, the fifth harmonic, which sounds E6 when the fundamental is C4; a step of the drawbar is about 3dB
Sets the level of the 1 1/3' sine, the sixth harmonic, which sounds G6 when the fundamental is C4; a step of the drawbar is about 3dB
Sets the level of the 1' sine, the eighth harmonic, which sounds C7 when the fundamental is C4; a step of the drawbar is about 3dB, despite the manual calling it the fifth harmonic
Sets how much third-harmonic percussion is added at the start of a note, a fast decaying tone a fifth and an octave above the fundamental
Sets how much second-harmonic percussion is added at the start of a note, a fast decaying tone an octave above the fundamental
Picks the decay time of the percussion tones, fast or slow
Turns key click on, which gates the sines on and off as fast as possible so the switching is audible; with it off the envelopes are slowed enough to stop the click
Sets the attack time of the note envelopes, which a Hammond does not have and which stands in for a swell pedal
Sets the release time of the note envelopes, which a Hammond does not have and which stands in for a swell pedal
Sets the pitch of each voice, a volt per octave; the number of channels on this cable sets how many voices play, and one voice plays with nothing patched
Opens the envelope for each voice while its gate is high; with nothing patched here every voice sounds continuously, which turns the module into a VCO
Multiplies the level of that drawbar, so 0V silences it whatever the drawbar is set to and a drawbar at zero stays silent whatever the voltage; the same voltage applies to every voice
Lengthens the attack of the note envelopes, added to the A knob so that the full range is reachable at any knob setting; the same voltage applies to every voice
Lengthens the release of the note envelopes, added to the R knob so that the full range is reachable at any knob setting; the same voltage applies to every voice
The organ voice, polyphonic with one channel per voice
Menu — factory presets grouped by the first word of the name: basics are pop, rock and jazz starting points, songs approximate Hammond recordings, and instrument names imitate other organ stops
squinkylabs-sines.notes: The manual's drawbar list omits 1 3/5' and 1 1/3' and calls 1' the fifth harmonic; the pitch table in composites/Sines.h gives the nine footages used here, and the lines follow it.

lines: Sampler that plays SFZ instruments, polyphonic, with velocity, exponential pitch modulation and through-zero linear FM using the samples as the carrier; an instrument is loaded from the context menu
Tunes the player over a two octave range
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the FM jack before it is added to the pitch knob
Sets the depth of the through-zero linear FM from the signal at the LFM jack
Sets the overall output level
Transposes the player in octaves over a ten octave range
Sets the pitch of each voice, a volt per octave with 0V as C4; the number of channels on this cable sets how many voices play
Sets the velocity of each note, 0V for MIDI velocity zero and 10V for velocity 127; what an instrument does with velocity varies, often picking between samples or setting the level
Starts a note while the voltage is above 1V and ends it below that, one channel per voice
Bends the pitch exponentially through the trim knob above it, positive voltage raising the pitch and negative lowering it
The modulator for through-zero linear FM, with the samples as the carrier; an audio rate signal is the usual thing to patch here
Scales the depth of the linear FM, 0V for none and 10V for the full depth set by the Depth knob; with nothing patched it acts as though 10V were present
The instrument's audio, polyphonic with one channel per voice
Menu — Load SFZ file opens a file picker for the instrument; the display at the top then shows its name and the range of pitches it answers to, or the error if it would not load
Menu — Trigger delay holds the gate input back by 5 samples, which is worth leaving on in most patches
squinkylabs-samp.notes: Params 0, 5 and 6, the key switch, the patch schema number and the trigger delay setting, have no control on the panel.

lines: Feed-forward compressor and limiter with two polyphonic channels, fixed ratios and knee shapes, makeup gain and a wet-dry mix for parallel compression; every channel shares the one set of settings
Picks the compression ratio and knee: Limit is an infinite ratio hard knee, then 2:1, 4:1, 8:1 and 20:1, each with a soft-knee and a hard-knee setting; a soft knee eases the way into compression
Sets the level above which the signal is compressed, in dB with 0dB at 10V; the lower it goes the more compression there is
Adds makeup gain to the output, 0 to 40dB, to bring the level back up after compression has pulled it down
Sets the attack time, 0 to 200ms; a very short attack compresses the transients as well as the body of the sound
Sets the release time, 0 to 2 seconds
Blends the compressed signal with the untouched one, 0 to 100% wet, which is how parallel compression is set up
Bypasses the compressor, connecting each input straight to the output beside it, for comparing the compressed and uncompressed sound
The audio into one of the two compressors, monophonic or up to 16 channels; the cable patched here sets that channel's polyphony
The compressed audio from that side, with the same number of channels as the input feeding it
Note — the meter shows gain reduction two decibels a segment, so a full meter is at least 16dB of reduction
squinkylabs-comp.notes: Output 2 has no position on the panel and no line.

lines: Sixteen channel feed-forward compressor and limiter for a polyphonic cable, with its own settings per channel, a side-chain input, makeup gain and a wet-dry mix for parallel compression
Picks which of the channels the panel controls are editing; the other channels keep their own settings
Picks the compression ratio and knee for the selected channel: Limit, which is an infinite ratio hard knee, then 2:1, 4:1, 8:1 and 20:1, each with a soft-knee and a hard-knee setting
Sets the level above which the selected channel is compressed, in dB with 0dB at 10V; the default is at the top, so it has to come down before anything is compressed
Sets the attack time for the selected channel, 0 to 200ms
Sets the release time for the selected channel, 0 to 2 seconds
Blends the compressed signal with the untouched one on the selected channel, 0 to 100% wet
Bypasses the selected channel, passing it through untouched; every channel starts this way
Adds makeup gain to the selected channel, 0 to 40dB
Takes the level that drives compression on the selected channel from the side-chain input rather than from the audio input
The audio to be compressed, one channel of the cable per compressor channel
The signal the gain detector reads on any channel whose SC button is on, one channel of the cable per compressor channel
The compressed audio, with the same number of channels as the input
Menu — Stereo mono picks Mono for sixteen independent channels, Stereo for eight pairs sharing settings, or Linked-stereo, where a pair shares its gain reduction so the image does not shift
Menu — Panel channels labels the meters and the channel display 1-8, 9-16 or Group/Aux to match a Mind Meld mixer, and changes nothing in the sound
Menu — Copy channel, Paste channel, Set all channels to current and initialize current channel move settings between channels without editing each one
Note — the gain reduction meter runs 18 decibels top to bottom, with lines drawn at 6dB and 12dB of reduction
squinkylabs-comp2.notes: Params 8 and 9 carry the stereo mode and the channel labelling from the menu and have no control on the panel. Output 1 has no position on the panel and no line.

lines: Transistor ladder filter with fifteen responses, five distortion voicings and a variable slope, plus control over where in the ladder the distortion happens; stereo, or sixteen polyphonic channels
Sets the cutoff frequency, 20Hz fully counter-clockwise to 20480Hz fully clockwise
Sets the resonance; it stops short of self-oscillation
Sets how hard the signal is driven into the filter, which is where most of the distortion comes from; a lot of it makes the response types other than lowpass lose their shape
Sets the output level, which is worth having because the other controls change the level a great deal; the lamps beside it follow the louder of the two channels, 6dB a step, with the red one at 7V
Moves the distortion between the four filter stages: equal gain at centre, more in the early stages counter-clockwise, more in the late ones clockwise; other responses need it centred
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Edge jack before it is added to the Edge knob
Picks the response: lowpass at one to four poles, bandpass at two and four, highpass at one to three, highpass and lowpass combinations, lowpass with a notch, an allpass, a notch and a phaser
Picks the distortion between the filter stages: Transistor is Moog-like saturation, Fold puts a wave folder before each stage, the Asym settings add even harmonics, and Clean has none
Simulates capacitors that are not matched, from exact at the minimum through values typical of a Moog to badly out; it is heard mostly as a loss of resonance
Sets how much the bass is preserved as the resonance rises: fully down gives the bass loss a Moog is known for, fully up removes it
Sets the slope of the four pole lowpass continuously between -6dB and -24dB per octave; the other response types ignore it and the slope lamps go dim
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Slope jack before it is added to the Slope knob
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the CV1 jack before it is added to the cutoff frequency
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the CV2 jack before it is added to the cutoff frequency
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Q jack before it is added to the resonance knob
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Drive jack before it is added to the Drive knob
Moves the cutoff frequency through the trim knob below it, tracking a volt per octave with that trim fully clockwise; it is summed with the other cutoff input, so two modulation sources need no mixer
Sets the resonance through the trim knob below it
Sets the drive through the trim knob below it
Sets the slope of the four pole lowpass through the trim knob below it; an inverted envelope here gives a bright attack that mellows
Moves the distortion between filter stages through the lone trim knob above the row of attenuverters
The audio into the left channel; the number of channels on this cable sets the polyphony, and with the right input unpatched this signal is filtered once and sent to both outputs
The audio into the right channel, which runs its own filter with the same settings; in polyphonic mode it is inactive
The left channel's filtered audio, with the same number of channels as the left input
The right channel's filtered audio
Menu — Stereo polyphonic turns the left channel into up to sixteen polyphonic channels and leaves the right side inactive, at a considerable cost in CPU
Note — a channel uses no CPU at all until both its input and its output are patched
Polyphonic state-variable filter with a choice of 12dB or 24dB slopes, lowpass, bandpass, highpass and notch responses, a built-in limiter, and a control that splits the resonant peak into two
Sets the centre frequency, 16.35Hz at the bottom of the travel and 16744Hz at the top; with R turned up it moves both peaks together
Sets the resonance
Splits the resonance into two peaks and sets how far apart they are; it does nothing in the 12dB setting, and in the Par - topology nothing comes out at all until it is turned up
Picks the topology: 12dB for one two pole filter, 24dB for two in series, Par for two in parallel, or Par -, the difference between them, which passes nothing until R is turned up
Picks the response: LP for lowpass, BP for bandpass, HP for highpass, N for notch

Turns on the limiter, which has a fixed threshold, attack and release and an infinite ratio; it holds the level steady through a filter sweep and is worth turning off for dynamics or for gating with R
Sets the output level; the lamps beside it show the level, and nothing aliases audibly while the red one stays off
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Fc jack before it is added to the Fc knob
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Q jack before it is added to the Q knob
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the R jack before it is added to the R knob
The audio to be filtered; the number of channels on this cable sets the polyphony
Moves the centre frequency through the trim knob above it, a volt per octave with that trim fully clockwise
Sets the resonance through the trim knob above it
Splits the resonant peak through the trim knob above it; an envelope here with the Par - topology makes the filter act as a gate
The filtered audio, with the same number of channels as the input
Menu — Alt Limiter makes the built-in limiter a little faster and a little different in sound
squinkylabs-f2.notes: Params 7, 9 and 12 hold the CV update rate, the patch schema and the alternate limiter setting, and have no control on the panel.

lines: Filter bank tuned to the formants of a singing voice, with the frequencies, bandwidths and gains taken from measurements of singers, held fixed rather than animated
Moves all the formant filters together, a volt per octave
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Fc jack before it is added to the Fc knob
Sets the resonance of the formant filters
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Q jack before it is added to the Q knob
Sweeps smoothly through the vowels A, E, I, O and U, with the lamps above showing which one is being sung
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the vowel jack before it is added to the vowel knob
Picks the voice the formants are modelled on: B for bass, T for tenor, CT for countertenor, A for alto, S for soprano
Raises the level of the upper formants: fully down leaves the gains the singing model gives them, which fall away with frequency, and fully up brings them level with the first formant
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Brite jack before it is added to the Brite knob
The audio to be filtered
Sets the resonance through the trim knob beside it
Moves all the formant filters through the trim knob beside it, a volt per octave with that trim fully clockwise
Sweeps through the vowels through the trim knob beside it
Raises the upper formants through the trim knob beside it
The filtered audio
Recreation of Bernie Hutchins's Vocal Animator: four bandpass filters at vocal formant frequencies, three swept by a bank of slow triangle LFOs, which morphs a rich input into vocal tones
Sets the speed of all four internal LFOs at once, keeping the ratios between them
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the LFO jack before it is added to the LFO rate knob
Picks how closely the four LFOs track each other: down keeps them closely correlated, the middle loosens them, and up lets them go their own ways
Moves the frequencies of the lower three filters, the lowest tracking a volt per octave and the middle two moving less; the top filter stays at 3700Hz
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Fc jack before it is added to the Fc knob
Sets the resonance of the filters, which sharpens or broadens each formant
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Q jack before it is added to the Q knob
Sets how far the summed LFOs move the filters, the lower filters moving further while the top one stays put
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Depth jack before it is added to the Depth knob
Adds bass by switching some or all of the filters from bandpass to lowpass
The audio to be filtered, which suits a harmonically rich source such as a low pulse wave or something distorted
Sets the LFO speed through the trim knob beside it
Sets the resonance through the trim knob beside it
Moves the filter frequencies through the trim knob beside it
Sets the modulation depth through the trim knob beside it
The four bandpass filters summed together; their unmodulated frequencies are 522Hz, 1340Hz, 2570Hz and 3700Hz
One of the internal triangle LFOs, for modulating other modules or as a slow random-looking voltage
squinkylabs-vocalanimator.notes: Param 9, Track ExP, has no control on the panel.

lines: Polyphonic stereo waveshaper with eight shapes, from gentle overdrive to wave folding and bit crushing, oversampled to keep aliasing out and switchable between AC and DC coupled outputs
Picks the shape: Smooth for a tube-like asymmetric curve, Clip for hard clipping, Emitter Coupled for 3080 chip saturation, Full Wave and Half Wave rectifiers, Fold and Fold 2 folders, and Crush
Boosts the signal going into the shaper, which is what brings on the shaping and distortion; on the rectifier shapes it only changes the level
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Gain jack before it is added to the gain knob
Shifts the signal before the shaper, which brings in even harmonics, and passes it untouched at centre; on Smooth it sets asymmetry instead, with none at the bottom of its travel
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the offset jack before it is added to the offset knob
Picks the oversampling: 16X for aliasing that is hard to measure, 4X for most of that at a quarter of the work, and 1X for none, which is right for shaping control voltages and for deliberate grit
Switches the outputs between AC, which runs them through 20Hz highpass filters to strip the DC an asymmetric shape makes, and DC, which leaves those filters out so control voltages keep their offset
The left channel's audio; patched on its own it is shaped once and sent to both outputs
The right channel's audio, shaped with the same settings
Drives the gain through the trim knob above it, which is where an envelope goes for a swept folder
Shifts the offset through the trim knob above it
The left channel's shaped audio
The right channel's shaped audio
Note — on the Crush shape the gain knob sets the bit depth, from 16 bits down to one bit as it is turned up
Note — a channel uses no CPU at all until both its input and its output are patched
Stereo frequency shifter after the Moog and Bode module: every frequency moves by the same number of Hz rather than by an interval, so harmonics land out of tune
Sets the shift by hand, -5 to 5, added to the voltage at the CV jack
The left audio to be shifted
The right audio to be shifted
Sets the shift, -5V for the largest downward shift and 5V for the largest upward one, added to the SHIFT AMT knob, despite the maker's tooltip naming it Disorder
The left channel shifted upwards
The left channel shifted downwards, which can fold frequencies below zero and produce a lot of subsonic energy
The right channel shifted upwards
The right channel shifted downwards, which can fold frequencies below zero and produce a lot of subsonic energy
Note — the RANGE button sets the span: 5 Hz, 50 Hz, 500 Hz or 5 kHz, each meaning that much down at the minimum and that much up at the maximum, or exp, which runs 2Hz to 2000Hz a volt per octave
Note — there is no anti-aliasing, so shifting up until the highest input frequency plus the shift passes half the sample rate will alias
squinkylabs-freqshifter.notes: The CV input is named Disorder in the maker's own tooltip; the panel and the manual both call it the shift CV, and the line follows those. RANGE is a choice button rather than a parameter, so it has no tag.

lines: Noise generator with a continuously variable spectrum slope, covering white, pink, red, blue and violet noise and everything between them
Sets the slope of the noise spectrum, -8dB per octave fully counter-clockwise to 8dB per octave fully clockwise, with the display below showing the spectrum
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the input jack before it is added to the slope knob
Sets the slope through the trim knob beside it
The noise; its slope is held flat below 40Hz and above 6000Hz, which keeps the extremes from running away
Random voltage source made from white noise run through a five band graphic equaliser at extremely low frequencies, so the mix of slow and less slow wandering is set band by band
Sets the base frequency of the equaliser, 0.1Hz to 2Hz, placing the five bands at that frequency and at two, four, eight and sixteen times it; each band's frequency is printed beside its knob
Sets how much of that band goes into the output, on an audio taper
Sets the gain of that band through the knob beside it
The random voltage, -5V to 5V, or 0-10V when the menu is set to unipolar
Menu — Extra Low Frequency moves the base frequency range down to 0.01Hz to 0.2Hz
Menu — Unipolar puts out 0-10V in place of the standard -5V to 5V
squinkylabs-lfn.notes: Param 6 holds the Extra Low Frequency menu setting and has no control on the panel.

lines: Two independent random voltage generators, each noise through a bandpass filter whose centre frequency and Q are set by knob and CV
Sets the centre frequency of that channel's bandpass filter, about 1Hz fully counter-clockwise to 4000Hz fully clockwise
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Fc jack for that channel before it is added to the Fc knob
Sets the Q of that channel's bandpass filter, 1 to 30, which narrows the band and makes the output more nearly a wandering sine
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Q jack for that channel before it is added to the Q knob
Moves the centre frequency of that channel's filter through the trim knob above it
Sets the Q of that channel's filter through the trim knob above it
That channel's filtered noise
squinkylabs-lfnb.notes: This module has no manual. Param 8 carries the Extra Low Frequency menu item, which in this build only changes how many digits the frequency display shows: the DSP never reads it. The frequency figures come from the composite, where the knob maps to 2 to 14 and the filter runs at two to that power divided by four.

lines: Tremolo built around an LFO that can be locked to an external clock and multiplied from it, with the raw and shaped LFO brought out to jacks of their own
Sets the speed of the internal LFO, which is used when the Clock knob is set to int
Picks the clock: x1, x2, x3 and x4 lock the LFO to the signal at the ckin jack at that multiple of its rate, and int runs the internal LFO at the Rate knob's speed
Rounds and then flattens the LFO waveform, which deepens the tremolo as it goes up
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the jack beside it before it is added to the Shape knob
Sets the asymmetry of the LFO: a symmetric triangle at centre, a rising sawtooth at one end and a falling one at the other
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the jack beside it before it is added to the Skew knob
Sets how far the synchronised LFO lags the external clock, which is how the tremolo is placed on or off the beat
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the jack beside it before it is added to the Phase knob
Shifts and scales the LFO before it modulates the audio, which deepens the tremolo as it goes up
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the jack beside it before it is added to the Depth knob
The clock the LFO locks to when the Clock knob is set to a multiple
The audio to be modulated
Shapes the LFO waveform through the trim knob beside it
Sets the LFO asymmetry through the trim knob beside it
Sets the phase against the external clock through the trim knob beside it
Sets the modulation depth through the trim knob beside it
The audio with the tremolo applied
The skewed sawtooth straight from the LFO, before the shaping
The LFO after shaping, which is the signal that modulates the audio
Clock divider that counts in gray code, so that only one output changes at each clock, with eight bit outputs and a weighted sum of them
Switches between the standard gray code, where the low bits change far more often than the high ones, and a balanced gray code, where every bit changes about as often as the others
The clock the counter advances on; there is no internal clock, so nothing happens until this is patched
One bit of the gray code counter, high or low, with the lamp beside it following it
All eight bits added together with binary weighting, which makes a stepped voltage out of the count
Turns a polyphonic CV and gate pair into eight separate gates, one for each semitone from C4 to G4, for driving drum modules or gating mixer channels from a sequencer
The pitch CV, quantised to semitones; a channel whose pitch lands on one of the eight semitones from 0V upwards raises that gate
The gate for each channel of the CV input, which raises the output belonging to that channel's pitch
Goes high while a channel is playing the semitone this jack belongs to, with the lamp beside it following it
squinkylabs-dt.notes: The output jacks are numbered from the bottom of the panel upwards: output 0 is C at the bottom and output 7 is G at the top. Param 0, named Test, has no control on the panel.

lines: Eight lag generators each with a VCA, for smoothing gates so that they do not click or for using a gate as an attack-release envelope, with a mixing scheme that groups any run of channels together
Sets the rise time shared by all eight lag generators
Sets the fall time shared by all eight lag generators
Sets the level of the mix outputs, on an audio taper
The gate or control voltage that channel smooths; left unpatched, the channel takes the signal from the nearest patched gate jack above it, so one gate at the top drives all eight
The audio that channel's VCA passes, scaled by the lag output; left unpatched it acts as a steady 10V, so the lagged gate itself comes out
Lengthens the rise time of all eight lag generators, added to the Rise knob
Lengthens the fall time of all eight lag generators, added to the Fall knob
That channel's audio input multiplied by its lag generator, or the lagged gate on its own when nothing is patched to that channel's audio input
A mix of that channel and of every channel above it whose own mix jack is unpatched, scaled by the Level knob
Polyphonic piano-roll sequencer of unlimited length, edited by mouse, computer keyboard or MIDI keyboard while it plays, with unlimited undo, MIDI file import and export and an end-of-cycle trigger
Tells the sequencer how to read the clock input, from x1 for one pulse a quarter note up to x96; it should match the ratio on the clock module, and it changes playback only, never the editing grid
Sets how many voices play at once, up to 16; notes beyond that steal a voice, and a setting of 1 is what gives true monophonic legato
Starts and stops playback, changing colour while it runs; the Run input does the same job, and either can start or stop it
Lets the note display scroll along with playback
Turns on step recording, so that a note played at the CV and Gate inputs is written at the edit cursor and the cursor then moves on by a grid unit
The clock that playback advances on, read according to the Clock rate setting
Returns playback to the start of the sequence
Starts and stops playback, for patching from the run output of a clock module
The gate side of step recording: a note is written while a gate is high, and the cursor moves on when every held note is released
The pitch side of step recording: it sets the pitch of the note written at the edit cursor
The pitch of the playing notes, a volt per octave, with as many channels as the polyphony setting
The gate for each playing voice; two touching notes of the same pitch are separated by dropping the gate for 1ms
A trigger each time playback reaches the end of the sequence and loops back
Menu — Hookup Clock finds a Clocked or CLKD module in the patch and wires its clock, run and reset outputs to this one
Menu — Enable remote editing makes this module the editor for the clip selected on a 4X4 sequencer, so that clicking a pad there brings that clip in here
Menu — Load midi file imports the first track in a standard MIDI file that has notes on it, and Save midi file writes the sequence out as a type-0 file
Note — the note grid has its own right-click menu carrying the grid, snap and articulation settings, and the keyboard drives nearly everything: the manual lists the commands
squinkylabs-sequencer.notes: Params 1, 2, 6 and 8 hold the tempo, an unused run and stop setting, the audition setting and the remote-edit flag, and have no control on the panel.

lines: Four track clip player: sixteen pads, a row per track and a column per section, each holding a clip that repeats a set number of times before the track moves on; clips come from Seq++ or the clipboard
Tells the player how to read the clock input, from x1 for one pulse a quarter note up to x96; it should match the ratio set on the clock module
Sets how many voices that track can play at once; 1 is what gives true monophonic legato
Picks what that track's CV input does: Next and Prev step forward or back on a rising edge, Set picks the clip by voltage at a volt per clip, and Poly reads all three from channels 1, 2 and 3
Queues the clip under that pad, and the whole column across all four tracks, to play next; control-click, or command-click on a Mac, queues that track alone, and the change comes at the clip's end
Starts and stops playback; a compatible clock module patched to the Run input drives this instead, and the two must agree
The clock that playback advances on, read according to the Clock rate setting
Returns every track to its first clip; while stopped it queues the first clip of each track to play
Starts and stops playback, for patching from the run output of a clock module
Changes which clip that track plays next, in the way its CV Function selector is set to read it
Picks any of the sixteen pads by pitch while its gate is high: the four semitones from the base octave are track 1's sections, the next four track 2's, and so on; the menu sets the base octave
The gate that tells the Sel CV input to act, one channel per voice, so several pads can be queued at once
The pitch of that track's playing notes, a volt per octave, with as many channels as its Polyphony setting
The gate for each of that track's playing voices
Menu — Hookup Clock finds a Clocked or CLKD module in the patch and wires its clock, run and reset outputs to this one
Menu — CV select base octave sets which octave of pitches the Sel CV input reads, counted in octaves of C
Note — right-clicking a pad gives it a menu of its own: cut, copy and paste for the whole clip, a repeat count that can be Forever, and commands to queue that section or open the clip in Seq++
Note — a pad is light green while its clip plays, dark green when it holds notes and is silent, grey when it is empty but has a duration, purple when selected, and outlined when queued next
squinkylabs-sequencer4.notes: Param 6, Trigger Immediate, is compiled out of the context menu in this build and does nothing. Param 27 holds the CV select base octave from the menu. Output 8 has no position on the panel and no line.

lines: Two sine oscillators, A and B, each with ten harmonics, and a grid of buttons ring-modulating any harmonic of A against any of B; everything switched on is summed and divided by the number switched on
Sets the base octave of that oscillator, five down to four up
Transposes that oscillator by up to 11 semitones either way
Adds that harmonic of oscillator A straight into the output
Adds that harmonic of oscillator B straight into the output
Adds the product of one harmonic of A and one harmonic of B into the output, which is a ring modulation of the two
Sets the pitch of oscillator A, a volt per octave
Sets the pitch of oscillator B, a volt per octave
Everything switched on, added together and divided by the number of things switched on
squinkylabs-ch10.notes: This module has no manual, no entry in the maker's docs folder and no tooltip names beyond 'some harmonic'; everything here was read from composites/CH10.h. The hundred grid buttons, params 20 to 119, are tagged to the ring modulation line: in the composite the button at column c and row r multiplies harmonic c of A by harmonic r of B. Params 124 and 125, the fine tune controls, have no position on the panel and no line.

lines: A blank panel with no controls and no jacks, which the maker ships as the starting point for building a new module
squinkylabs-blank.notes: Param 0, named Test, has no control on the panel.
